newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn says uncertainty on taxes blocking investment.
newsitem.headline: Bonn says uncertainty on taxes blocking investment.

text.p: Uncertainty about planned reforms of the German tax and social security systems is the main factor holding back investment needed to jump-start the domestic economy, the Economics Ministry said on Wednesday.

In its latest monthly economic report, the ministry repeated its forecast that gross domestic product probably grew slightly in the first quarter of 1997, but said growth was still driven by exports while domestic demand was sluggish.
The report suggested that domestic investments were being kept on hold until the details of government reforms that could affect the viability of these projects were made known.

"This is particularly true for the final definition of reforms of the tax and social security systems," the report said. "That is why it is urgent that we have clarity quickly so that investment plans can begin with a sound basis."
The report added that all available economic data currently point towards a continued recovery of the economy.
The most recent survey of business confidence by the Munich-based Ifo economic research institute showed that companies were more optimistic about the future than in the past.

Industry orders over the past two months have also improved, particularly from abroad, although domestic orders during the same period have fallen slighlty. Industry production has begun to clearly expand.
